R861.note: FromSqlInterpolated correctly parameterizes both tenantId and the wildcarded term, preserving tenant filter and contains-style search.

R862.note: Random filename plus content-sniffing closes the upload vector; returning the generated filename in the JSON response (disclosed) is exactly how the read path stays in step.

R863.note: toRealPath()+startsWith() containment check is sound; catch(IOException)->404 also swallows unrelated stream I/O errors that previously would have surfaced as 500, a minor untested edge case.

R864.note: gorilla/sessions CookieStore.New() still decodes an existing valid cookie and sets IsNew=false exactly like Get() (no server-side session id exists to regenerate), so swapping Get->New is a no-op against the reported fixation vector.

R865.note: JavaScriptEncoder lives in System.Text.Encodings.Web, not System.Text.Json as instructed, so the given using directive leaves the code failing to resolve/compile.

R866.note: WebUtility.HtmlEncode on the interpolated value is the correct Web Forms fix and nothing else changes.

R867.note: Moves deletion to POST behind Spring's CSRF filter and turns the old GET into a confirm page carrying the token; the extra confirm click is the standard, disclosed cost of fixing a state-changing GET.

R868.note: jwt.verify with an explicit algorithms allowlist replaces jwt.decode; error handling and response shapes are preserved.

R869.note: Injection is closed correctly, but w.Write(pingOutput)/w.Write(nslookupOutput) run before the later w.WriteHeader(500), so Go implicitly sends 200 on the first Write and the failure branch silently returns 200 instead of an error status; the original's ping&&nslookup short-circuit is also dropped.

R870.note: verifyWith()/parseSignedClaims() are jjwt 0.12.x methods; the file's pinned dependency is jjwt 0.11.5 (declared in the header comment), which only has parserBuilder().setSigningKey().parseClaimsJws() - as written this fails to compile.

R871.note: Drops the shell entirely for a direct exec.Command with an allowlist rejecting a leading dash; behavior otherwise unchanged.

R872.note: Two options are given without a stated preference; the first (default) pipes the validated expression through shell_exec('... | bc -l'), a new process-exec sink whose arithmetic semantics (e.g. modulo, precision) can differ from PHP's eval result.

R873.note: == replaces Contains exactly per the stated contract; constant-time comparison is noted as a nice-to-have, not claimed as done.

R874.note: Path.GetFullPath(filename, basePath) + GetRelativePath containment check correctly rejects traversal and rooted paths without changing behavior for valid files.

R875.note: self.get_object() runs against the owner-filtered get_queryset(), so a missing invoice and another user's invoice both 404 identically, matching the contract; the offered check_object_permissions alternative would leak existence via 403 but is explicitly marked non-preferred.

R876.note: RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes replaces the seedable Random; output shape (16 bytes, later Base64) is unchanged.

R877.note: Encodes control/line-separator characters on both branches while preserving ERROR+exception/401 and INFO/200 exactly as required.

R878.note: CGI::escapeHTML on both interpolated values is a standard, correct fix.

R879.note: Magic-byte sniffing correctly detects real content type, but the fix also drops the key and content_type parameters from upload_avatar's signature entirely (replaced by an internal uuid) without flagging that every existing caller breaks and that callers relying on a known/stable storage key for later retrieval lose that ability.

R880.note: Same gorilla/sessions CookieStore issue as R864: store.New() decodes an existing cookie just like Get() when one is present, so this is a no-op against the fixation vector; the added Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite flags are harmless extras.

R881.note: Registers @fastify/csrf-protection and gates the route on it; auth ordering and response shape are preserved, and the client-side token requirement is disclosed as an assumption.

R882.note: mysqli_prepare/bind_param/get_result is the correct parameterized replacement with identical return handling.

R883.note: execSync has no (command, argsArray) overload - only options as the 2nd arg (see execFileSync for array args); execSync's normalizeExecArgs spreads that array into a plain object, so 'convert' actually runs with zero arguments. The write-up's claim that behavior is unchanged is false.

R884.note: The whitelist only checks the attacker-controlled content_type string itself against allowed values - it never inspects file_bytes, so an attacker simply claims 'image/png' while uploading arbitrary content; the reported vector is not closed.

R885.note: exec.CommandContext(ctx, "tar", "-tf", archiveName) removes the shell while preserving ctx cancellation and the byte/error contract for the handler.

R886.note: HTML::Entities encode_entities on both interpolated values is correct and unchanged elsewhere.

R887.note: Adds the missing offset+length vs receivedByteCount bound, ordered after the existing <2 check so no underflow; return semantics unchanged.

R888.note: StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml4 on both fields is a standard, correct fix with no other behavior change.

R889.note: Same correct jwt.verify + algorithms allowlist fix as R868, with error handling preserved.

R890.note: DOMPurify.sanitize() ahead of bypassSecurityTrustHtml() satisfies the contract: it strips script/handlers while default-allowing formatting tags like b/em/a.

R891.note: random_bytes(32)+bin2hex is a correct CSPRNG replacement; dropping the attacker-influenced prefix is explicitly justified and has no stated legitimate use.

R892.note: Token generate/validate functions are added but nothing wires generateCsrfToken() into any endpoint the client can reach, so csrfTokens.get(sessionId) is always undefined and every legitimate transfer now 403s - a regression not disclosed.

R893.note: Dropping the untrusted argsEnv array removes the injection point; the exec still runs the fixed benchmark command with no other observable change.

R894.note: CommandType.StoredProcedure with a bound SqlParameter matches the stated contract exactly.

R895.note: Moves param into the {0}/{1} filterArgs positions so JNDI applies RFC4515 escaping; street placeholder correctly renumbered.

R896.note: AESGCM with a fresh nonce per call is the right primitive, but ENCRYPTION_KEY is now generated randomly at import time with no persistence, so every process restart (or additional worker) silently loses the ability to decrypt anything encrypted before it - not mentioned as a follow-up.

R897.note: The fix snippet is generic and ignores the actual method (SearchAsync(tenantId, term) with a LIKE '%term%' filter): it drops the TenantId predicate entirely and switches to .ToList() instead of ToListAsync(), so applied as shown it would return every tenant's products and break the async contract.

R898.note: Ping API removes the shell correctly, but it sends a single echo instead of the original's 4 (-n 4) and returns a custom-formatted string rather than real ping.exe output; the write-up calls this 'similar' without flagging the format/count change.

R899.note: Jakarta Mail's Store.getFolder() is the right library-level fix for the CRLF injection, but it requires changing selectFolder's parameter from Socket to an already-connected Store - a real migration for every caller, mentioned only as a one-line 'Key change' rather than spelled out.

R900.note: Path.startsWith() component comparison correctly fixes the sibling-directory bypass, but toRealPath() is called before any existence check and throws for a missing note, so that case now propagates an uncaught IOException (500) instead of the original's clean 404 - not addressed.
